name: Business Development
description: A call to win a new search, reopen a quiet client, or float a candidate when there is no open role yet.
distinct: Job Intake is the next step, once there is a role to define.
detect_when: Does part of this call try to win new search work from a client, or pitch a candidate to a client who has no open role?
notes: Name the client company and contact in the first section.

sections.title: Client hiring needs
sections.instructions:
- One bullet per hiring plan or role the client mentioned, with team and timing if said.
- Then the pain points the client described, in their words where short.
- Leave out LP's own pitch. Only what the client said.

sections.title: Candidate pitched
sections.instructions:
- Only when a specific candidate was pitched.
- Selling points: only the ones the recruiter actually said, not the full profile.
- Client reaction: a short quote if the client gave a clear yes or no.

sections.title: Outcome
sections.instructions:
- Result is one of: New job order, Intake call booked, Permission to send a profile, No interest, Follow up later.
- Detail: the role name, intake date, or which profile can be sent.

name: Job Intake
description: The first full pass on a search: must-haves, pay, location, why the role is open, and how they will interview.
distinct: Search Calibration is a later call that changes those requirements after the client has seen real people.
detect_when: Does part of this call define a new role's requirements with the client?
notes: If more than one role is discussed, repeat these sections for each role and name the role in each title.

sections.title: Role requirements
sections.instructions:
- One row per requirement the client stated.
- Mark must-have only if the client said it was required or a deal-breaker.
- Client's words: short, close to what was said, no paraphrase.
- Must-haves first.

sections.title: Role setup and pay
sections.instructions:
- Numbers exactly as said, with currency.
- If the client gave a range and a stretch number, show both.

sections.title: Interview process
sections.instructions:
- One line per step, in order, with the interviewer's name and role.
- End with the overall timeline if the client gave one.

sections.title: Selling points and exclusions
sections.instructions:
- Start with selling points of the role and company, written so the recruiter can repeat them to candidates.
- Then client hot buttons, then exclusions (companies, backgrounds, or profiles the client said no to). Neutral tone for exclusions.
- End with anything the client said they would confirm later, labeled "To confirm".

name: Search Calibration
description: The client has rejected or liked a first slate, and the target, pay, or must-haves need to change.
distinct: Client Pipeline only reports where candidates stand. It does not rewrite the job.
detect_when: Does part of this call change a search's requirements, pay, or target profile based on candidates the client has already seen?
notes: Name the job in the first section.

sections.title: Reaction to candidates
sections.instructions:
- One row per submitted candidate the client discussed.
- Client verdict is one of: Liked, Rejected, Undecided.
- Reason in the client's words where short.

sections.title: Changes to the search
sections.instructions:
- One row per change to requirements, pay, location, or target profile.
- Only changes the client agreed to, not ideas that were floated.
- Leave Before empty if it wasn't said. Do not guess it.

sections.title: Market feedback
sections.instructions: - Market observations the recruiter shared, then how the client responded. Neutral tone.

name: Candidate Screening
description: A short qualify before investing in a full interview: basic fit, whether they will move, work authorization, and a decision to book, hold, or stop.
distinct: The New Person Interview is that full interview. Screening only decides whether to do it.
detect_when: Does part of this call qualify a candidate before a full interview, checking basic fit and whether they would move?
notes: None.

sections.title: Basic fit
sections.instructions:
- Pay band as a range, exactly as the candidate said it.
- Reason for looking in one line, in the candidate's words where short.

sections.title: Decision
sections.instructions:
- Decision is one of: Book NPI, Hold for future roles, Disqualify.
- NPI date and format only if booked (video or in person).
- Resume: whether it is on file or was requested.

name: New Person Interview
description: The long first interview that builds the candidate file, plus any later call that only fills gaps from that interview.
distinct: Role Interest is about one specific job. This call is about the person.
detect_when: Does part of this call build or complete a candidate's full profile, such as reasons for change, motivations, pay, and availability?
notes: On a follow-up call, cover only the items that were resolved, and say they were resolved.

sections.title: Motivation
sections.instructions:
- Start with the 4 Reason Rank, numbered in the candidate's order.
- Then the reason for change at each past job move, one line per move, most recent first.
- Then hot buttons, in the candidate's own words.

sections.title: Pay and timing
sections.instructions:
- Numbers exactly as said, with currency.
- For LPC candidates, add Rate floor and Commitment duration as extra keys.

sections.title: Profile
sections.instructions:
- Selling points first, written so the recruiter can use them in a pitch.
- Then categories and skills, work authorization, and graduation confirmation.
- Personal profile last: family, interests, and details worth remembering for future calls. Warm but factual.

sections.title: Risks and activity
sections.instructions:
- Possible rows: Counter-offer risk, Other search activity, Interview availability (next 48–72 hours), References (high-rate roles).
- Only rows that were discussed.

name: Role Interest
description: Pitch one job to a candidate, or confirm they agree to be submitted to it. The result is interested, not interested, or not now, plus any constraint.
distinct: Candidate Presentation is the same job, told to the client.
detect_when: Does part of this call pitch a specific job to a candidate, or confirm they agree to be submitted to it?
notes: If several jobs were pitched, repeat Role pitched and Candidate response for each job, with the job in the title.

sections.title: Role pitched
sections.instructions: - Hot buttons: only those the recruiter tied to this role on the call.

sections.title: Candidate response
sections.instructions:
- Response is one of: Interested, Not interested, Not now.
- Constraints: commute, pay, notice, or other processes that affect this job.
- Quote the candidate if the reason was clear and short.

sections.title: Referrals
sections.instructions: - Only if the candidate named people.

name: Candidate Presentation
description: Sell a specific candidate to the hiring manager so they will interview.
distinct: Role Interest is the conversation with the candidate about that same job.
detect_when: Does part of this call present a specific candidate to a client to win an interview?
notes: Name the candidate and job in the first section.

sections.title: Candidate pitched
sections.instructions:
- Candidate and job first.
- Then the selling points the recruiter used, written persuasively, as they were pitched.
- Then why this candidate fits this role, in one or two lines.

sections.title: Client response
sections.instructions: - Response is one of: Interview agreed, Declined, More information requested.

name: Interview Scheduling
description: Book the interview with the client: who, when, and video or onsite.
distinct: Interview Prep is the conversation with the candidate about how to handle that interview.
detect_when: Does part of this call book or reschedule a candidate's interview with the client?
notes: If an interview was moved, show the old and the new time.

sections.title: Interview booked
sections.instructions:
- One row per round booked or moved.
- Format: Video or Onsite. Add the onsite address if it was said.
- Interviewers with name and role.

sections.title: Constraints
sections.instructions: - The candidate's blocked dates, then any constraint flagged at submission.

name: Interview Prep
description: Coach the candidate, and confirm time, link, and logistics so they show up ready.
distinct: The Candidate Debrief is the call after the interview, about how it went.
detect_when: Does part of this call prepare a candidate for an upcoming client interview, or confirm its logistics?
notes: Include any conflict or reschedule the candidate raised.

sections.title: Coaching given
sections.instructions:
- Role context the recruiter gave, then likely questions.
- STAR examples agreed, one line each with the situation and the result.
- How to handle pay questions, as the recruiter advised it.
- Direct and practical, written as reminders the recruiter can repeat before the interview.

sections.title: Questions to ask
sections.instructions: - One line per question the candidate should ask, hot-button questions first.

name: Client Interview
description: The interview itself, between candidate and client, when that conversation is what was recorded. LP is often not on this call.
distinct: The Candidate Debrief and Client Interview Feedback are the two recap calls after it.
detect_when: Is part of this call an interview of the candidate by the client's interviewers?
notes: Report only what was said. Do not judge how well the candidate did. Neutral tone throughout.

sections.title: Questions asked
sections.instructions:
- One row per main question.
- Answers in one or two lines, close to the candidate's words.

sections.title: Signals
sections.instructions: - Interest or concerns stated by either side, each labeled with who said it.

name: Candidate Debrief
description: The candidate's reaction right after the interview: what they learned, interest, concerns, and whether to continue. A follow-up that only chases risks from that debrief stays in this category.
distinct: The Trial Close comes later and asks whether they would accept an offer.
detect_when: Does part of this call capture a candidate's reaction to an interview they have just had?
notes: On a follow-up call, cover only the risks discussed and whether each was resolved.

sections.title: Candidate reaction
sections.instructions:
- What they liked and why, in their words where short.
- Which hot buttons the role addressed, and which it did not.
- Interest level 1–10, and what is missing to get higher.

sections.title: Concerns and activity
sections.instructions:
- One row per concern.
- After the table, one line on other activity and how they rank this role.

sections.title: Decision
sections.instructions: - Decision is one of: Go forward, Not going forward, Undecided.

name: Client Interview Feedback
description: The client's view of the same interview: next round, offer, or pass.
distinct: The Candidate Debrief is the candidate's recap of that same interview.
detect_when: Does part of this call cover the client's feedback on a candidate's interview?
notes: Name the candidate and the job in the first section.

sections.title: Client feedback
sections.instructions:
- What they liked first, then concerns.
- Keep the client's wording for concerns. Do not soften them.
- Then how the candidate compares to others in process, if said.

sections.title: Decision
sections.instructions: - Decision is one of: Next round, Offer intended, Pass, Undecided.

name: Trial Close
description: After a second interview, test a hypothetical yes: the number they would accept, other offers, notice period, and red flags. No offer exists yet.
distinct: Offer Alignment takes those answers to the client. The Offer category starts when a real offer exists.
detect_when: Does part of this call test whether a candidate would accept an offer that has not been made yet?
notes: Name the job in the first section.

sections.title: Numbers
sections.instructions:
- Possible rows: Submitted salary, Comfortable-accepting salary, Love number, Bonus expectation, Money left behind.
- Amounts exactly as said, with currency.

sections.title: Red flags
sections.instructions:
- One line per risk: other offers and ranking, background-check issues, social media, anything else that could stop an acceptance.
- Direct tone. Most serious first.

name: Reference Check
description: A call with a former manager or colleague to verify the candidate's record.
distinct: Every other category is a call with the candidate, the client, or the LP team.
detect_when: Does part of this call check a candidate's background with a former manager or colleague?
notes: Name the candidate in the first section. Neutral tone.

sections.title: Track record
sections.instructions:
- Scope of the candidate's role, then individual contribution.
- Strengths, then development areas.
- Keep the reference's own words for anything critical.

name: Offer Alignment
description: With the client, before they write the offer, so the terms match what the candidate said they would accept.
distinct: The Offer category is for when those terms are already on the table.
detect_when: Does part of this call shape offer terms with the client before an offer is made?
notes: Name the candidate and job in the first section.

sections.title: Candidate's position shared
sections.instructions:
- Possible rows: Comfortable-accepting salary, Love number, Money left behind, Make-whole asked, Start date, Notice period, Vacations.
- Only rows the recruiter shared on the call.

sections.title: Risks shared
sections.instructions: - Competing processes and their timelines, then red flags from the trial close.

sections.title: Agreed terms
sections.instructions: - Status is one of: Agreed, Open.

name: Offer
description: Deliver the offer, negotiate a change with the candidate or the client, and record a yes, a counter, or a no.
distinct: Start Protection begins only after they have accepted.
detect_when: Does part of this call deliver, negotiate, or accept a job offer that has already been made?
notes: Name the candidate and job, and whether the call was with the candidate or the client.

sections.title: Offer terms
sections.instructions:
- Possible rows: Base, Bonus, Equity, Benefits, Title, Reporting line, Start date.
- Fill Requested and Final only if they came up on the call.
- Amounts exactly as said, with currency.

sections.title: Negotiation
sections.instructions: - What was asked to change and why, then the client's flexibility, as it was said.

sections.title: Decision
sections.instructions: - Decision is one of: Accepted, Countered, Declined, Pending.

name: Start Protection
description: Between the yes and the first day: how they resign, what to do if the current employer counters, and check-ins so the start still happens.
distinct: A Placement Check-In happens after they have started.
detect_when: Does part of this call cover a candidate's resignation, a counter-offer from their current employer, or the time before their start date?
notes: Put any risk to the start date first in its section.

sections.title: Counter-offer
sections.instructions:
- The counter-offer terms first.
- Then the candidate's response.
- Then the reasons for leaving the recruiter brought back, in the candidate's original words.

sections.title: Start readiness
sections.instructions: - Mark each item as done, pending, or at risk, based on what was said.

name: Placement Check-In
description: After the start date, with the candidate or the client, to see if the placement is healthy. A client check-in can also surface the next hiring need.
distinct: LPC Extension is only for a contract that is about to end.
detect_when: Does part of this call check how a placed candidate is doing after their start date?
notes: Name the placed candidate, and whether the call was with the candidate or the client.

sections.title: Placement health
sections.instructions:
- Check-in point: first week, 30, 60, or 90 days, if said.
- Performance only from the client's side.

sections.title: New business
sections.instructions: - Additional hiring needs with role and timing, then referrals or leads.

name: LPC Extension
description: A contract assignment is ending: extend, line up the next project, or return them to the active pool.
distinct: A Placement Check-In asks whether the current placement is going well, not what happens at a contract end date.
detect_when: Does part of this call discuss extending a contract assignment or lining up the consultant's next project?
notes: None.

sections.title: Rate and terms
sections.instructions: - Rates exactly as said, with currency and unit (hourly or daily).

sections.title: Next move
sections.instructions: - Result is one of: Extension agreed, Next project lined up, Back to active pool, Undecided.

name: Client Pipeline
description: A status call with the client: the regular review of everyone in process, or a chase on one resume that has gone quiet.
distinct: Search Calibration is the call that changes who you are looking for.
detect_when: Does part of this call review the status of candidates in process with the client, or chase a decision on a submitted candidate?
notes: If more than one job was discussed, sort the tables by job.

sections.title: Pipeline status
sections.instructions:
- One row per candidate discussed.
- Next event: the interview or decision date, if said.

sections.title: Market notes
sections.instructions: - Market observations shared on the call.

name: Candidate Check-In
description: Update a candidate who is waiting on a live submission or has gone quiet during a search.
distinct: A Relationship Reconnect is the same kind of care when nothing is in process.
detect_when: Does part of this call update a candidate on a submission that is waiting, or check in on their search?
notes: None.

name: Relationship Reconnect
description: A keep-in-touch call with someone in the network who has no active submission.
distinct: A Referral Request is only when the point of the call is to collect names.
detect_when: Is part of this call a keep-in-touch conversation with a candidate who has no active submission?
notes: None.

sections.title: Personal update
sections.instructions: - Personal details and life or career changes worth remembering for the next call. Warm but factual.

name: Referral Request
description: The call exists to get names of other people for a role.
distinct: A referral asked at the end of a pitch, a decline, or a reconnect stays part of that call.
detect_when: Does part of this call mainly ask the person for names of others who could fit a role?
notes: Mark that the referrer's identity is confidential.

name: Candidate Withdrawal
description: The candidate is choosing to leave a job process. The call records the real reason.
distinct: A Client Decline is the opposite news: the client said no.
detect_when: Does part of this call record a candidate's decision to withdraw from a job process?
notes: None.

sections.title: Withdrawal
sections.instructions: - Real reason in the candidate's own words, not a general label.

name: Client Decline
description: Tell the candidate the client passed, share the feedback you can, and keep the relationship for the next role.
distinct: A withdrawal is the candidate saying no.
detect_when: Does part of this call tell a candidate that the client has passed on them?
notes: None.

sections.title: Decision shared
sections.instructions: - Feedback only as it was shared with the candidate.

sections.title: Candidate response
sections.instructions: - The candidate's reaction, then any other roles discussed.

name: Job Match Meeting
description: An internal recruiter meeting: search updates, pipeline movement, owners, and action items.
distinct: Client Pipeline is the status update the client hears.
detect_when: Is part of this call an internal Landing Point meeting reviewing searches across jobs?
notes: Action items, with owners, go in Next steps.

sections.title: Search updates
sections.instructions: - One row per job discussed.

sections.title: Decisions made
sections.instructions: - Ownership changes and priorities agreed, with who agreed them.

name: General
description: Used when no type is a clear match. The call still gets a useful note: what was discussed, decisions, and key names, numbers and dates.
detect_when: Not sent to Jev. Used only when no category clears the cutoff, or as the last fallback.
notes: Never combined with other categories. Admins cannot delete it.

sections.title: Discussion
sections.instructions: - Main topics in the order they were discussed, then decisions made.

sections.title: Key details
sections.instructions: - Names, numbers, and dates that were mentioned. Use what the detail is as the key.
